calls.reason: The May 6, 2025 Lacey v. State Farm order found nonexistent authorities in a brief, and counsel's declarations traced them to AI tools. That shows the problem was still reaching courts when he wrote.

Business Insider, drawing on Charlotin's data, reported at least 23 court findings of AI hallucinations from May 1 to 27, 2025, with lawyers at fault in 13. That is close to one a day, a pattern rather than an anomaly.

An archive snapshot hours after the post shows 112 cases, about 0.87 a week since ChatGPT's launch. It lists 19 May decisions against 15 in April, and BI counted 73 in early 2025 against 37 in all of 2024, so the pace was rising.

Only one documented case of a lawyer saying she was shocked (Ko v. Li), and a later tribunal found she misled the court. The Butler Snow lawyers apologised rather than showed surprise, and no survey isolates brief drafting, so 'many' is unsupported.
